name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default.

This lets keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks instantly, solving a core keyboard navigation failure. The trade-off is a small visual footprint—we accept a fixed-position element that’s always present, but its size and contrast ensure it’s unmissable.

name: Reader
text: A large, always-visible skip link steals focus from the main content for sighted users on page load, harming sighted keyboard users who tab through. A skip link that only appears on focus risks being invisible to screen-reader users who don’t tab immediately. Test both patterns with a screen reader and keyboard—if sighted keyboard users can’t skip without tabbing twice, and screen readers can’t reach it at all, the pattern fails.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link that only appears when keyboard focus reaches the top of the page**. This solves the problem for screen-reader users who navigate by focus, not sighted keyboard users who tab through. The trade-off is a brief visual flash—we accept that sighted keyboard users might notice the skip link appear, but it’s a small price for universal accessibility.

name: Reader
text: A skip link that only appears on focus fails sighted keyboard users who rely on visual cues—they won’t see it until they’ve already tabbed past navigation blocks, defeating the purpose. Instead, use a skip link that’s always present but visually subtle (e.g., small, low-contrast), then expands to high-contrast on focus. Test with both screen readers and keyboard-only users to confirm it’s discoverable without distracting sighted users.
